basics.name: Yifan Kang
basics.label: Undergraduate researcher, MIT
basics.summary: Junior at MIT studying AI (6-4) and Mathematics (18), advised by Leslie Kaelbling. Interested in robots that learn efficiently at deployment time, and in combining coding agents with robot foundation models.

work.name: 2077AI
work.summary: Agentic systems for few-shot robot manipulation.
highlights: Encore: a coding agent turns three demonstrations into an executable policy program and repairs it from its own execution traces. Oral, NeurIPS 2026 Robot Learning Workshop.
Deployed coding agents on robots to perform bimanual tasks in the real world.

work.name: MIT
work.summary: With Prof. Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Learning & Intelligent Systems group.
highlights: KeyFlow (CoRL 2026 Workshop Learn@Deploy): a coding agent adapts a manipulation policy by rewriting how a few demonstrations are represented and retrieved, with no retraining.
62.6% mean held-out success on 13 RoboCasa tasks, against 47.8% for a VLA fine-tuned on ten times more demonstrations.

work.name: MIT
work.summary: With Prof. Antonio Torralba, on visual generation with multimodal LLMs.
highlights: Co-first author of Doodle Agent: Exploring Freeform Visual Generation with Multimodal LLMs (Accepted to ICCV 2025 AI4VA Workshop), a drawing agent for open-ended visual creation using LLMs and structured prompting.

volunteer.position: Explore HRT — Algorithm Development (Quantitative Research) track
volunteer.summary: Invite-only program. Implemented a limit order book and an arbitrage strategy from scratch; ranked 4th of 15 by PnL.
One of 24 students invited nationwide to a quantitative trading competition.
Authored CNOT-Optimal Circuit Synthesis under the mentorship of Henry Ma (MIT); selected as a top-5 paper out of 100.
Three years of mentored research on NUMA-aware concurrent data structures, alongside advanced mathematics.

awards.title: MIT CSAIL Agentic AI Hackathon — Winner (Jane Street Award)
awards.summary: For Fireroad.ai, an AI course planner for MIT students. Award included presenting the project at Jane Street in New York.

publications.name: ENCORE: Few-Shot Agentic Discovery of Manipulation Strategies
publications.summary: A coding agent reads three demonstrations, writes an executable policy program, and repairs it from its own execution traces.

publications.name: Interpreting Diffusion Language Models Over Denoising Time
publications.publisher: CoLM 2026 Workshop on Non-Autoregressive Language Models
publications.summary: Sparse autoencoders and cross-layer transcoders for diffusion LLMs, with timestep-aware tracing and causal interventions.

publications.name: KeyFlow: Agentic Policy Adaptation with Episodic Memory
publications.summary: Co-first author (equal contribution with Ben Zandonati). A coding agent adapts a manipulation policy by rewriting how a few demonstrations are represented and retrieved, beating a VLA fine-tuned on ten times more data.
